title: Hungary removed the Commission copy, but kept the national noise-declaration copy
statusLabel: Residual national copy duty; legal significance under review
deadlineLabel: EU application date; adoption/publication due 28 November 2025
summary: The national-only submission remains after Hungary’s 2025 partial repeal. Its compatibility requires legal review.
nationalGap: Section 11(1) still requires a copy for every equipment type. The 2025 amender deleted only Section 11(2), the Commission route.
nationalLaw: Government Decree 140/2001, Section 11(1); amending Decree 469/2025, Section 2.
consequence: Yes, on paper. Manufacturers or EEA representatives still owe the Government Office routine copies. No actual submission, refusal or penalty is established.
resolution: No later removal of Section 11(1) located.
caveat: This is a residual-text lead, not a finding that every national information duty is unlawful. The underlying directive’s harmonisation/free-movement rules support scrutiny, but lawful market-surveillance requests remain available. The national rule states no advance-submission deadline; no premarketing condition or automatic fine is inferred. Declaration preparation, retention, targeted requests and actual administrative practice are separate.

comparison.before: Copy to Government Office for every type.

review: Independent primary-law comparison, authentic amender and adverse legal-scope review passed. The coordinating researcher separately read the live current national version. Legal significance and actual enforcement remain qualified.
recognitionNote: Government publications acknowledge the broader reporting reform. No published source identifying this precise surviving national-only copy duty as an implementation mismatch was located; no first-discovery claim.

noveltySearch.method: Bounded exact identifier and Hungarian reporting/error searches across official sources and public commentary found enactment, explanatory memorandum, draft and generic reform summaries; none identified the precise residual national-copy mismatch.
